reasons: Only the first twelve sections were visible, so the remaining routes cannot be judged.
Access control for these routes is not visible in the code shown.
The cancel route changes only the database status, and whether background work actually stops is not visible here.

terms.meaning: A web address path that the app answers, and what it does when called.
A written rule for the shape a request or response must have, here checked with the zod library.
One step in a lessons-learnt run, such as gathering facts, each with its own saved result.
The industries, segments or projects the user has chosen to work on.
A downloadable record of the sources, facts and stage results from a run.
The presentation built from a run's results, shown in a viewer.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the lessons-learnt routes
sections.what: Brings in the web router, validation, database access, research helpers, run helpers, export functions and deck tools that the routes in this file use.
sections.why: Reason not stated for each import. The file is the place where the tool's web routes are assembled.
sections.watch_out: The file depends on many other folders, so moving or renaming any of them breaks these routes.

sections.name: V3_HEAVY
sections.title: List of heavy stage names
sections.what: Lists the stage names whose stored data is large. The summary endpoint leaves these out and expects clients to fetch them from the result endpoint.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps summary responses small. The comment says the result endpoint serves these stages instead.
sections.watch_out: A new heavy stage must be added to this list, or it will bloat every summary response.

sections.name: lightSummary
sections.title: Removing heavy stages from summaries
sections.what: Returns a run's summary with the heavy stage entries removed. A missing summary is passed back as missing.
sections.why: Likely reason: follows from the heavy list above, to keep responses small.
sections.watch_out: Callers must expect a missing summary to come back as nothing rather than an empty object.

sections.name: use
sections.title: Attaching presentation routes
sections.what: Adds the presentation routes from another file to this router.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps slide-related endpoints in their own file.
sections.watch_out: In Express, route order matters, so the position of this line can change which route answers a request.

sections.name: use
sections.title: Attaching the deck viewer routes
sections.what: Adds the standard deck viewer routes for the lessons-learnt deck, labelled as Lessons Learnt. The comment says this gives the same viewer, assistant, proposals and export as Reality Scan.
sections.why: The comment explains that the same deck tools are reused for this tool.
sections.watch_out: Changing the deck storage functions changes what this viewer saves and loads.

sections.name: post
sections.title: Cancelling a run
sections.what: Lets the user stop a run that is queued, running, failed or interrupted. It marks the run as cancelled, marks any running stages as cancelled, and keeps the results already completed. Finished runs return a conflict error.
sections.why: The error text says completed checkpoints and evidence are kept, so cancelling never throws away finished work.
sections.watch_out: The code only changes database status, so whether background work actually stops depends on the runner, which is not visible here.

sections.name: get, precheckBodySchema
sections.title: Downloading the research ledger and check shape
sections.what: Builds a downloadable JSON record of a run: its stage results, a research workbook built from the ledger and facts when both are valid, and a source bundle. Returns 404 if the run has no stages. It also defines the shape used to check a preview request.
sections.why: The notice in the response explains that historical stage summaries are kept unchanged and that candidate counts are not verification counts.
sections.watch_out: If the ledger or facts fail validation, the workbook is set to nothing without any error message.

sections.name: createRunBodySchema
sections.title: Shape of a run creation request
sections.what: Defines the required request contents for starting a run: a scope and optional project names.
sections.why: Likely reason: the request is checked before a run starts, so bad input is rejected early.
sections.watch_out: The scope rules come from another file, so a change there changes what this route accepts.

sections.name: previewBodySchema
sections.title: Shape of a preview request
sections.what: Defines the same request contents as the run creation step, so a preview uses exactly the input a run would use.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeping the two shapes the same means a preview matches the run it predicts.
sections.watch_out: Two copies of the same shape can drift apart if only one is edited.

sections.name: exportBodySchema
sections.title: Shape of an export request
sections.what: Defines the request contents for an export: a scope, optional project names, and an optional file name slug.
sections.why: Likely reason: the export needs a name for the file, and the slug is optional.
sections.watch_out: The slug is used only when it is supplied, and the export step falls back to a default otherwise.

sections.name: narrowScopeToProjectNames
sections.title: Narrowing a scope to chosen projects
sections.what: If project names are supplied, reduces the scope to only the matching Yard projects. It throws an error if nothing is in scope or no name matches, and clears the industry and segment lists.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets a user pick individual projects from a list instead of whole industries.
sections.watch_out: Because industries and segments are cleared, the narrowed scope depends only on the matched project ids.

sections.name: post
sections.title: Previewing a recipe
sections.what: Builds a recipe preview from the scope and returns the full recipe plus a short list of pillars with their fact counts. Bad input returns 400, and other failures return 500 with the error message.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the user see the recipe's structure before starting a full run.
sections.watch_out: Non-scope errors send their raw message to the caller, which could expose internal details.

sections.name: post
sections.title: Export scope for the Recipe agent
sections.what: Packages the chosen Yard projects into a flat data set that the separate Python Recipe service can read. The reply includes a note telling the caller to send the saved database path to that service.
sections.why: Likely reason: the Recipe agent runs as a separate service and needs its input in a fixed shape.
sections.watch_out: The reply note hard-codes the Recipe service address and port, so that text goes stale if the service moves.

sections.name: post
sections.title: Check a scope before running
sections.what: Takes a scope, resolves it against the Yard, and returns the result without starting a run. Bad input gets a 400 reply with a validation code.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the user see what a run would include before starting one.
sections.watch_out: Validation errors and server errors return different codes, so callers must read the code field and not only the status.

sections.name: get
sections.title: Search projects by name
sections.what: Returns up to 20 projects whose name contains the typed text, sorted by name. Input shorter than two characters returns an empty list.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the project picker fast and small.
sections.watch_out: The typed text goes into a pattern match without escaping, so percent signs and underscores act as wildcards.

sections.name: post
sections.title: Start a new lessons run
sections.what: Checks the scope, narrows it to the chosen project names, creates a run record, and starts it in the background. Returns the new run and its precheck with a 201 status.
sections.why: Likely reason: the run is recorded first, so its progress can be tracked even if starting it fails.
sections.watch_out: If the background start fails, only a log line is written and the caller still gets success, so the run can sit idle until someone kicks it.

sections.name: get
sections.title: List the latest runs
sections.what: Returns the 20 most recent runs, newest first, as full run records.
sections.why: Likely reason: provides a short history list for a screen.
sections.watch_out: The limit is fixed at 20, so older runs cannot be reached through this route.

sections.name: get
sections.title: Load one run with its stages
sections.what: Returns one run, its stage results in order, and which engine produced it. For the newer engine, stage summaries are trimmed. An unknown run returns 404.
sections.why: Likely reason: the newer engine stores lighter summaries, so the code shapes the reply differently for each engine.
sections.watch_out: The reply has two shapes depending on the engine field, so any screen must check that field first.

sections.name: get
sections.title: Get the finished recipe-v3 result
sections.what: Returns the saved result for a run that finished under the newer engine. If none exists, returns 404 with a not-ready code.
sections.why: Likely reason: the result is saved once so the page does not have to rebuild it.
sections.watch_out: The not-ready code also applies to runs on the older engine, so a missing result does not always mean the run failed.

sections.name: get
sections.title: Serve the pinned demo run
sections.what: Returns details of the recorded run that the guided demo replays. It is refused with a 409 and the list of problems if the pinned run no longer matches the Yard.
sections.why: The code comment says this keeps the demo from replaying a stale set of projects.
sections.watch_out: The pin is checked on every request, so any change to the Yard's projects makes the demo refuse until the pin is updated.

sections.name: get
sections.title: Show the evidence ledger for a run
sections.what: Returns the coverage ledger for a run: counts by item type, counts per pillar, counts by routing basis, and up to 2,000 item rows that can be filtered by kind, project or pillar.
sections.why: The code comment says the ledger records each item the run used and where it went.
sections.watch_out: The item list stops at 2,000 rows and sets a truncated flag, so a screen that ignores that flag will show incomplete data.

sections.name: get
sections.title: Download the methodology as PDF
sections.what: Builds a methodology note as a PDF for a finished recipe-v3 run and sends it as a file download named with the first eight characters of the run ID. Returns 404 if no result exists.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The download name uses the first eight characters of the run ID from the address, and the ID is not checked beyond that.

sections.name: post
sections.title: Restart a run in the background
sections.what: Asks the background runner to kick a run again so it can resume. Returns whether it resumed. An unknown run returns 404, and other refusals return 409.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets someone resume a run that stopped partway through.
sections.watch_out: Both the already-succeeded case and the other refusals return the same 409 status, so the special case is not separated in the reply.

sections.name: get
sections.title: Download the slide deck
sections.what: Builds and sends a PowerPoint file for a succeeded run. It uses the saved scene deck if one exists, then the newer engine's render, then the older recipe render. A run that is not finished or has no saved recipe gets a 409.
sections.why: The code comment says the file is rebuilt from the database, never from data the browser posts.
sections.watch_out: Three separate rendering paths can produce slightly different files, so a fix in one path may not reach the others.

sections.name: tool
sections.title: Register the route module
sections.what: Packages the router with a short slug and a title so the main app can mount it as the Recipe for Success tool.
sections.why: Likely reason: the app finds and mounts tools through this default export.
sections.watch_out: The slug is how the app identifies this tool, so renaming it can break links and mounting.

summary: Defines the web routes for the lessons-learnt tool, which let the app preview a recipe, export data, cancel runs, download research records, and read run results. Only part of this file was available, so this description is partial.
purpose: Connects the lessons-learnt features to the web address paths the front end calls.
why: Likely reason: a single router file keeps all lessons-learnt endpoints in one place, and the comments explain a few specific choices such as keeping heavy results out of the summary.
how: It sets up shared request checks, a helper that hides heavy stage data, and then defines each route. The cancel route marks a run as cancelled, the ledger route builds a downloadable record, the preview route builds a recipe preview, and the export and deck routes are attached from other files.
inputs: Request bodies with a scope and optional project names, and run ids taken from the web address.
outputs: JSON responses for runs, previews and summaries, a downloadable research ledger file, and error responses with a status code and message.
risks: Within the visible code, no check of who is calling is shown, so access control must be confirmed elsewhere. Preview errors send the raw error message back to the caller. Route order matters, so an earlier route can catch requests meant for a later one.
debug: If a route returns 400, check the request body against the schema for that route. If the ledger returns 404, check that the run has recorded stages. If a preview fails with 500, read the server log line that starts with lessons-learnt. If a cancel returns 409, the run is missing or already finished.
